newsitem.title: FRANCE: French plane evacuates foreigners from Kisangani.
newsitem.headline: French plane evacuates foreigners from Kisangani.

text.p: A French air force transport plane landed at a small airstrip in the Zairean city of Kisangani on Saturday to evacuate 15 foreigners as rebels overran the city's main airport, a Defence Ministry spokesman said.

The C-160 Transall plane, arriving from Bangui in the Central African Republic, had 30 French paratroopers aboard for protection when the plane reached the ground but there were no incidents, a spokesman said.
The French plane left for Bangui with seven French nationals, one Belgian, a Swiss and six Africans of separate nationalities employed by non-government organisations on board, the spokesman said.
The operation took place as looting broke out in the city, the former Stanleyville, and rebels overran the international airport outside town.

Prime Minister Alain Juppe ruled out a unilateral French military intervention in Zaire, saying: "We do not intend to launch again a solely French operation and, after all, we do not have all the means to carry it out either,"

France has been pressing for a multinational peace force to be sent to Zaire to ensure aid supplies got through the refugees. Critics say the real aim is to prop up President Mobutu Sese Seko, a long-time ally of Paris.
Juppe told Canal-Plus television France still hoped for the creation of a multinational force to establish security areas where humanitarian aid could be distributed.
"France cannot do everything by itself, be it in Zaire or in Albania," said Juppe.
He said Paris backed United Nations efforts to bring about a cease-fire and the departure of foreign troops from Zaire.

France's most notable intervention to prop up Mobutu was in 1977 when it sent hundreds of foreign legion paratroopers to retake Kolwezi, capital of mineral-rich Shaba province, which had been invaded by Cuban-trained rebels.

The United States, now squabbling with Paris over policy towards Zaire, then supplied the aircraft which airlifted the legionnaires from Corsica to Zaire for a dramatic jump over Kolwezi where rebels were starting to kill foreign civilians.
